stories.title: Human bodies produce 2 billion metric tons of CO2 a year just by staying alive
summary: Humans collectively produce more than 2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide annually just by turning food into energy, a 74% increase over three decades largely driven by population growth.
Unlike fossil fuel emissions, however, the CO2 we exhale is part of the natural carbon cycle, and scientists say measuring it more accurately could improve climate models.

stories.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state.
The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.

stories.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
summary: Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky.
The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust.
Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.

stories.title: New Forest wildfire restoration work begins
summary: Work begins to restore nature to part of the New Forest destroyed by a summer wildfire.

stories.title: One of the year's most prolific meteor showers to light up the night sky this weekend
summary: The Leonid meteor shower, known for its bright and fast meteors, will kick off this weekend and continue until the end of November.

stories.title: A dead star's mysterious rings reveal what could happen when our Sun dies
summary: Astronomers have discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star, revealing a possible preview of our Solar System's distant future.
The two rings are separated by a mysterious gap that researchers believe is maintained by surviving planetary bodies, including one potentially as large as Pluto or the Moon.
Their different chemical compositions suggest they may contain the remains of separate destroyed planets.

stories.title: Scientists accidentally solve a chemistry mystery that lasted 60 years
summary: After more than 60 years of unsuccessful attempts, scientists have finally isolated stable examples of elusive boron-oxygen molecules once considered too unstable to capture.
The surprising breakthrough, achieved using relatively simple chemical reactions, could pave the way for an entirely new class of exotic compounds.

stories.title: How climate change worsens heatwaves, droughts, wildfires and floods
summary: Rising global temperatures mean extreme weather events are becoming more common and more intense.

stories.title: A really simple guide to climate change
summary: Human activities are causing the world to heat up, posing serious threats to people and nature.

stories.title: What is the Paris Agreement and why does 1.5C matter?
summary: The 2015 pact is at the heart of the international commitment to tackle rising global temperatures.

stories.title: What is net zero and is the UK on track to achieve it?
summary: Reaching net zero carbon emissions worldwide is essential to limit global warming, UN scientists say.

stories.title: Wales scraps controversial Uganda tree-planting scheme
summary: The Welsh government has given more than £4m to the scheme since 2015, but will end it due to budget pressures.

stories.title: US rockets firm eyes up mothballed Highland spaceport
summary: Colorado-based Leap is looking at the spaceport near Tongue as its first launch site outside of the US.

stories.title: Scientists just found dinosaur blood that survived 115 million years
summary: Scientists have discovered chemically confirmed traces of ancient blood inside 115-million-year-old dinosaur bones, challenging assumptions about how long biological molecules can survive.
The extraordinary preservation could unlock new clues about dinosaur physiology and even help scientists search for ancient life elsewhere in the universe.

stories.title: Could you live on a remote island as a job?
summary: The new manager will start each workday surrounded by nature at the island wildlife reserve.

stories.title: Five-inch-long beetle larvae are quietly destroying blueberry roots
summary: Scientists have solved a mystery surrounding destructive beetles attacking blueberry bushes in North Carolina, identifying a species whose massive larvae can grow up to five inches long and destroy plant roots.
Although farmers have reported damage for more than a decade, the insects responsible remained unidentified until researchers used DNA analysis to uncover the culprit.
